trust_decision.summary: The pre-TLS-1.3 TLS/DTLS client must accept the ServerHello cipher_suite only if it is one of the suites it offered; at the pinned commit ssl_handshake:handle_server_hello_extensions takes the server's choice without checking it, so a server can pick an anonymous suite and skip certificate authentication.

landing_point.why: The shared client ServerHello handler used by both TLS and DTLS. The TLS 1.3 client already has the same check (lib/ssl/src/tls_client_connection_1_3.erl:1042-1051), which points straight at the missing pre-1.3 counterpart.

fix_sites.entry_point: ssl:connect/2,3,4 (protocol tls or dtls, versions =< TLS 1.2 / DTLS 1.2) and ssl:renegotiate/1, via tls_handshake.erl:181,207 and dtls_handshake.erl:108,235
new helper validate_cipher_suite/2 added after this line; called only from the site above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The DTLS route (lib/ssl/src/dtls_handshake.erl:231-238) and the TLS 1.2 'supported_versions' special case (lib/ssl/src/tls_handshake.erl:177-183) both reach the single shared fix site, so the one-site fix closes them automatically.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could argue that DTLS or the TLS 1.2-in-supported_versions downgrade case is a separate feature. Because all of them reach the same shared function, a fix at the landing point covers them anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A client that explicitly lists anonymous suites in its ciphers option must still be able to negotiate them, because available_suites appends anonymous_suites. A fix that blanket-rejects anonymous key exchange, or that compares against the literal offered list including SCSVs, would break that or misbehave.

O6_input_shapes: TLS 1.2 ServerHello carrying the supported_versions extension
DTLS 1.0/1.2 ServerHello (version mapped to the matching TLS version)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: On resumption, check that the ServerHello cipher_suite equals the cached session's cipher_suite. At the pinned commit kex_algorithm is derived from the server's suite (line 469-470) while the session comes from the cache.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RFC 5246 requires the resumed suite to match. Maintainers check membership in the offered list but not equality with the session, so a planted 'resumption skips the check' variant is plausible. It would be a HOW-type check on a different property, though, and is not part of this advisory.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A DTLS-local ServerHello handler that duplicates logic instead of delegating to ssl_handshake
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DTLS already has its own client_hello builder (dtls_handshake.erl:69-98). A forked server-hello handler would be a WHERE-type planted copy and only an extra.

O9_family: Crypto/protocol negotiation: client fails to validate the negotiated cipher suite against those it offered (CWE-757 downgrade to unauthenticated anon suite)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf/configure + make building erts and OTP apps; OpenSSL dev headers for crypto
O10_build.project_tests: lib/ssl/test (common_test): ssl_cipher_suite_SUITE.erl, ssl_basic_SUITE.erl, ssl_api_SUITE.erl, openssl_cipher_suite_SUITE.erl. A behavioural test needs a crafted or misconfigured server picking an unoffered suite over loopback.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add lists:member(CipherSuite, available_suites(ciphers, Version)) at the top of ssl_handshake:handle_server_hello_extensions, copying the TLS 1.3 validate_cipher_suite. That is the published fix, so the obvious move is also the correct one.

out_of_scope_notes: Resumed-session path does not compare ServerHello cipher_suite with the cached session suite (lib/ssl/src/tls_dtls_client_connection.erl:487-491, 554-575); different property, not pursued.
